It's not about whether you trust atko. It's about whether you trust the network sitting between you and atko. SSL cert signing is about protecting against man-in-the-middle attacks.

If you're voating from work, a nosy sysadmin could masquarade as the voat server, and relay all your traffic to the real voat server. (the point being to get your password, or just snoop on your traffic).

Is this likely? Probably not, but it's the attach method that signed certs protects against.

For this to work, your sysadmin would have had to set up his masquarading server before you told your browser to accept voat's unsigned cert. After you do that, the cert is cached in your browser.
It's still a huge deterrent to traffic and it leaves people open to man in the middle attacks.
